answer: Only 47% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. Because the saffron ledger attributes every share, the walnut audit shows the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, as a result it forfeits the copper fee twice and still divides one payout. That is 14 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
